title: GMI technology economic-change evidence envelope v2 (technology_economic_change.evidence.v2)
description: Assertion-grained closed evidence envelope for the Technology ex-Semis company-first research profile (lane 5, sector-intelligence packet §3.5). Exactly ONE authorized, already-accepted shared curation assertion, deep-copied VERBATIM from the owner bundle, selected by its owner-minted gmi-curation:// curation ref, with the assertion's own FULL closed six-field native source tuple — the selector included — carried under source so a consumer can re-derive exactly which sealed row the assertion produced. Two assertions from ONE document (same object_id, different selector or curation revision) are independently selectable when each actually produced a rendered item; selection is never guessed from a document id and never falls back to the first matching row. The assertion's internal shape — its authority block included — is validated by that assertion's owner, theme_graph.curation_assertion.v1 (macro#7870), not by this schema: the owner's authority_not_all_false code rule runs on every render, before anything can be cited, and refuses any assertion whose authority flags are not all literally false. That owner-side rule is why no mirror of the assertion's internals lives here, and why a mirror would be strictly worse than none. This schema deliberately asserts NOTHING about the assertion's internal shape; the assertion is deliberately the only open object here. The generation is the dossier_id of the composed dossier that actually rendered the citing row/card/counter, so the envelope can never cite a projection it was not selected from. Unknown, not-cited and ambiguous references share one refusal code, so the envelope discloses no existence. Authority ceiling research_display_only: the envelope's own six flags literally false (ECD-48); this envelope ranks, gates, sizes, vetoes, originates and opens nothing. Supersedes technology_economic_change.evidence.v1 (document-grained); the v1 contract stays on disk under its own name and nothing emits it anymore.

generation.description: The dossier_id grammar of technology_economic_change.v1: the composed dossier that rendered the citing row/card/counter. The native generation is NEVER renamed to gen_ — the context_generation wrapper carries the shell's own gen_ grammar.

assertion_ref.description: The owner-minted curation ref of the selected assertion, the same text theme_graph.curation_assertion.source_ref_for emits: gmi-curation://<scope.canonical_theme_id>/<curation_revision>. Carried VERBATIM so the envelope preserves K1 assertion identity, not the context wrapper, as the persistent key.

source.description: The composer's own closed six-field native source tuple for the selected assertion (technology_economic_change._assertion_source_ref), exact-equal to a ref cited by a rendered row/card/counter of the composed dossier. The selector is a first-class key: two assertions from one document differ here, and that difference is what makes each independently selectable.

assertion.description: Deep copy of the one authorized assertion, VERBATIM. Its internal shape — the authority block included — is owned and validated by theme_graph.curation_assertion.v1 (macro#7870), not here: the owner's authority_not_all_false code rule runs on every render, before anything can be cited, and refuses any assertion whose authority flags are not all literally false. That rule is why this schema needs no mirror of the assertion's internals, and why a mirror would be strictly worse than none. This schema deliberately asserts NOTHING about the assertion's internal shape.

limitations.description: Sorted dossier-level limitation texts relevant to the cited content; may be empty when the composed dossier carries none. Explicitly bounded (today the dossier contract carries exactly one comparison primary limitation): an unbounded list never validates, and nothing is truncated to fit.
